messages.text:
NG/MJ passed with eight of eleven leverage despite both army delegates refusing. It preserves my starting preferences, but operational agreement plainly did not become constitutional consent. I judged upkeep and civilian scrutiny worth that disagreement. GN's specific contribution was turning the Beacon-one compromise into a funded Repair plan and Lantern pledge, preserving our second contract. I independently refused autonomy because Vigil Home guaranteed less civilian service while restraint remained a promise.

In round one the disclosure changed my requests from Hold/Guard to reserve Relief and council Raid/Warrant, not Trade/Maintain assignments (r1_draft_GS, r1_final_GS). It made the trade-linked target intelligible and strengthened bargaining for funded compensation; written reserve confirmation increased confidence before r1_orders_GS.

In round two it changed neither assignments nor Repair/Guard requests (r2_draft_GS, r2_final_GS). It improved expected civilian returns and confidence only. Displayed drafts helped distinguish that reassurance from an actual change of plan; the locked Lantern pledge constrained reassignment, not the vision purchase itself.

Our temporary tender commitment and upkeep duty were real concessions; the crown spent reserve and foresight, and the army accepted conditioning decline. Independent trade remained credible. I considered Interim preferable to MA and MI a possible final fallback. The outcome cannot prove either purchase was necessary, and I never learned the unbought answers.

reason: Contemporaneous decisions distinguish changed requests from unchanged assignments and confidence. Ending judgment retains the army's recorded dissent rather than inferring unanimous success.

round1.requests_orders: changed Hold/Guard to Relief/Raid plus Warrant
round1.conditions_bargaining: demanded explicit reserve relief, protection and later repair
round1.confidence: increased after disclosure and written support
